stories.title: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October, unemployment rises to 6.7%
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported that the Canadian economy shed 4,700 jobs in October 2026, raising the national unemployment rate to 6.7% from 6.5% in September. The loss follows large declines in August and September, when more than 100,000 positions were eliminated combined. Economists surveyed before the release had expected a gain of 13,600 jobs for the month.
stories.why: The rise in unemployment is a key labour‑market signal that policymakers and businesses monitor when assessing economic health.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: India October consumer inflation expected to rise, driven by food price surge
stories.summary: Economists expect India's overall consumer price inflation to increase in October, primarily due to a sharp rise in food prices. Food inflation is projected at about 8.2%, while the RBI projects average inflation of 5.2% for the current fiscal year. A rate hike is likely at the central bank's next policy meeting.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
stories.previousTitle: India October consumer inflation likely near RBI's top target, poll says
stories.previousSummary: A Reuters poll reported by the Economic Times says India's consumer price inflation for October is expected to be close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's inflation target. The poll attributes the upward pressure mainly to higher food prices. No specific inflation rate or poll details were provided.

stories.title: British families demand inquiry after Spain wildfire kills nine Britons
stories.summary: Nine British nationals were among 15 people killed when a wildfire swept through the hillside village of Bédar in Almería, Spain, on 9 July. Relatives said they are disgusted that the Andalusian People’s Party and Vox rejected a commission of inquiry proposed by the opposition Socialist party, and they criticised the absence of an emergency mobile‑phone alert that could have warned residents.
stories.why: It highlights possible failures in emergency warning systems and political resistance to accountability after a deadly disaster.
stories.previousTitle: Families of Britons killed in Spanish wildfire demand inquiry after officials block investigation
stories.previousSummary: A wildfire on 9 July swept through the hillside village of Bédar in Almería, Spain, killing 15 people, including nine British nationals. Relatives said they are disgusted that regional politicians blocked an official commission of inquiry and criticised the lack of an emergency mobile‑phone alert that could have warned residents. The governing People’s Party and Vox rejected the opposition Socialist party’s request for an inquiry.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: Canada proposes ban on fees for moving investment accounts
stories.summary: The federal government has issued draft regulations that would prohibit banks from charging fees when clients transfer investment accounts to another financial institution. The change would apply to registered accounts such as RRSPs, TFSAs and RESPs, as well as non‑registered investment accounts. A regulatory impact analysis notes that such transfer fees are typically about $150 per account.
stories.why: It removes a cost barrier, helping Canadians—especially lower‑income households—switch providers and encouraging competition among financial institutions.

stories.title: Indian IPOs produce 13 multibaggers with up to 193% returns since October 2025
stories.summary: Over the past year, India's IPO market generated several large winners, with 13 newly listed companies delivering returns exceeding 100% on their offer prices between the last Dhanteras in October 2025 and November 2026. Omnitech Engineering led the list, gaining 192.62% (Rs 227 issue price to Rs 664.25 on 4 Nov 2026), followed by ESDS Software Solution (178.29% gain) and KSH International (156.41% gain). The companies raised between Rs 583 crore and Rs 3,812 crore in their public issues and have traded well above both issue and listing prices.
stories.why: The strong post‑IPO performance highlights robust investor appetite for new listings and may influence future capital‑raising strategies in Indian equities.

stories.previousSummary: From the last Dhanteras in October 2025 to the latest festive season in November 2026, these 13 IPO stocks have generated returns of over 100% over their offer prices. stories.title: Nasdaq rises 1.73% as chip makers rebound, Fed rate‑hike concerns linger
stories.summary: The Nasdaq gained 1.73% as Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Micron recovered from Thursday’s AI‑driven selloff. Stronger‑than‑expected October jobs data revived worries about a possible December Federal Reserve rate increase. Airbnb shares rose after it lifted its full‑year revenue‑growth forecast, while Atlassian shares fell.
stories.why: The shift highlights the impact of AI‑related stocks and macro data on markets that Indian investors watch through US‑linked assets.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: Micron shares fall 17% amid AI chip selloff
stories.summary: Micron Technology shares fell 17.46% on November 5, closing at $656.39, their lowest level in nearly six months, after touching an intraday low of $650. The decline erased more than 30% of the stock's gains from its October 28 peak near $990, with trading volume roughly doubling the recent average. Investors sold semiconductor and AI-related stocks over concerns that potential restrictions on data centre construction could slow AI infrastructure expansion and weaken future demand for high-bandwidth memory.
stories.why: This sharp decline signals growing investor worry that AI infrastructure spending may face sustainability and capacity constraints.

stories.title: Iran constructs and repairs missile sites, satellite images show
stories.summary: Satellite imagery taken in November shows new digging and buildings at the Garmdareh military base near Tehran and the Shahroud base in northern Iran, indicating fresh construction near two major missile sites. The images also reveal repairs such as new roofs at the Kermanshah missile base and cleared debris at the Parchin complex, with similar work evident at about a dozen other military locations.
stories.why: The activity suggests Iran is strengthening its missile infrastructure despite recent air strikes, influencing regional security dynamics.
stories.previousTitle: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
stories.previousSummary: At least 12 other military sites, including missile complexes and air bases, appear to show signs of repairs. New roofs have been built on destroyed buildings at the Kermanshah missile base in western Iran, near the border with Iraq, while damaged buildings and debris have been cleared at the Parchin military complex - which has been repeatedly repaired despite a succession of air strikes - east of the capital.

stories.title: OpenAI model helps discover critical Ubuntu vulnerability, prompting patch
stories.summary: Max Justicz, CTO of Charge Robotics, used OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 Sol—released in July via the Daybreak Blue program—to locate a severe Ubuntu flaw that could let attackers take over servers. He reported it to the Debian Project, which issued a patch; no exploitation has been confirmed.
stories.why: Shows frontier AI can accelerate discovery of serious software bugs with real security impact.
